transcript.content: Hello, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?
I keep getting hit out of nowhere with that scene—my cousin on the pavement. I can hear the shouting, see the lights again, even when I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal.
Did you witness your cousin die?
I—what keeps coming back is seeing him on the pavement. The shouting, the lights... it just hits me again when I’m at the church office.
Were you there when your cousin was found on the pavement?
I keep seeing him there on the pavement. It comes back out of nowhere—the shouting, the lights—and I’m right back in it, even at the church office.
Were you physically there when your cousin was lying on the pavement?
I’m not sure—I just keep seeing it in my head. I can’t tell what’s memory and what’s the image coming back.
Did you actually see your cousin lying on the pavement in real life?
I—I keep seeing him on the pavement like it’s happening again. The shouting, the lights. It hits me even when I’m just standing in the church office trying to act normal.
How long have these scenes of your cousin on the pavement been coming back like this?
Since my cousin was killed—two years and three months now.
When that scene suddenly comes back, do you also get a sudden wave of intense panic?
It’s not just then. Most days I wake up with fear, anger, and guilt already sitting in my chest. Like I failed God, my family, and the kids who trusted me.
Do you avoid reminders of your cousin’s death?
Yeah. I take the long way around town so I don’t have to go past the community center or the court. And if someone starts talking about that night, I usually shut it down or find a reason to leave.
When that scene comes back, do you know it’s a memory, or does it feel like it is actually happening right then?
It feels real for a moment. I’m back there seeing him on the pavement, hearing people shouting and the lights—then I realize I’m standing in the church office trying to act normal.
Do you believe that your cousin died because of something you did or failed to do?
Yes. I keep thinking if I’d ended the event sooner, walked him out myself, or kept a better watch on those boys, he’d still be here.
Have you been feeling depressed most of the day nearly every day?
Most days, yeah. I wake up with this fear and anger and guilt already sitting in my chest. It feels like I failed God, my family, and those kids who trusted me.
Have you heard a voice when no one was there speaking to you?
No, I haven’t heard voices when nobody was there.
Have you been jumpy or easily startled?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed being especially jumpy.
Do you have nightmares about what happened to your cousin?
I’m not sure. I don’t really remember having nightmares specifically about that.
Do you often feel constantly on guard, like you need to watch for danger?

Yeah. I can’t sit with my back to a door anymore. At church events, I’m always watching people’s hands, the corners of the room, cars slowing down outside, and where the closest exit is instead of really paying attention to the people in front of me.
Have you felt unable to feel close to other people?
Yeah. Even when I’m surrounded by people at church calling me brother and asking me to pray, I feel like I’m behind glass. Like nobody can really reach me.
Have you lost interest in things you used to care about or enjoy?
Yeah. I used to love preaching, playing keys, taking pictures, even running ball with the guys. Now I either just go through the motions or avoid it. None of it feels alive in me anymore.
Have you been thinking that you would be better off dead or thinking about killing yourself?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Did you actually witness your cousin lying on the pavement that night?
Yeah. I saw him on the pavement. It keeps coming back to me out of nowhere—the shouting, the lights, all of it—even when I’m at the church trying to act normal.
Do you believe God is punishing you for your cousin’s death?
I don’t know if God is punishing me, but I keep blaming myself. I think if I’d ended things earlier, walked him out, or kept a better eye on those boys, he’d still be here.
